{{short description|American statistician and sociologist (born 1935)}}
'''Judith M. Tanur''' is an American [[statistician]] and [[sociologist]] who is Distinguished Teaching Professor Emerita of Sociology at [[Stony Brook University]].<ref name="stonybrook">[http://www.stonybrook.edu/commcms/sociology/people/faculty/tanur.html Faculty profile], [[Stony Brook University]], retrieved 2016-09-24.</ref>

Judith Tanur was born to Edward Mark and Libbie Berman Mark on August 12, 1935, in Jersey City, New Jersey.<ref>{{citation|title=Birth Notice 1 – no Title|work=New York Times|date=Aug 14, 1935|page=19|id={{ProQuest|<!-- insert ProQuest data here -->}} }}</ref> When Tanur was young, her family moved from [[New Jersey]], where she was born, to [[Great Neck, New York]].{{citation needed|date=May 2026}} She graduated from Great Neck High School in 1953 and entered [[Antioch College]], studying psychology and statistics there, but in 1955 she transferred to [[Columbia University]], in part because it was closer to the [[University of Pennsylvania]] where her future husband was studying dentistry. At the same time, she took a job at the New York State Psychiatric Institute. Tanur completed a bachelor's degree in [[psychology]] in 1957 and began graduate studies at Penn but became pregnant and dropped out. Eventually, she returned to graduate school, completed a master's degree in [[mathematical statistics]] from [[Columbia University]] in 1963, and took a new job as an editor for [[William Kruskal]] at the ''International Encyclopedia of Social Sciences''. She became a lecturer at Stony Brook in 1968, still only holding a master's degree,<ref name="hats">{{citation|url=http://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2012/09/01/tanursept2012/|title=Judith Tanur: A Woman of Many Hats|date=September 1, 2012|first=Jessie|last=Biele|magazine=Amstat News|department=Statisticians in History}}.</ref> and later completed her [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in sociology at Stony Brook.<ref name="stonybrook"/>

With S. James Press, she is the author of ''The Subjectivity of Scientists and the Bayesian Approach'' (Wiley, 2001; Dover, 2016).<ref>Reviews of ''The Subjectivity of Scientists and the Bayesian Approach'':
* {{citation | last = Gruber | first = Marvin H. J. | date = August 2002 | doi = 10.1198/004017002320256503 | issue = 3 | journal = [[Technometrics]] | pages = 292–293 | title = none | volume = 44| s2cid = 207015422 }}
* {{citation|last=Hox|first=J. J. | title = none|year=2002|journal=[[Journal of Official Statistics]]|volume=18|issue=2|pages=305–307|hdl=1874/25681 }}
* {{citation | last = Woodward | first = P. | date = March 2003 | doi = 10.1111/1541-0420.00267 | issue = 1 | journal = [[Biometrics (journal)|Biometrics]] | pages = 204–205 | title = none | volume = 59}}
* {{citation | last = Edwards | first = A.W. F. | doi = 10.1002/sim.1488 | issue = 13 | journal = [[Statistics in Medicine (journal)|Statistics in Medicine]] | pages = 2237–2238 | title = none | volume = 22 | year = 2003}}
* {{citation|url=http://www.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/the-subjectivity-of-scientists-and-the-bayesian-approach|work=MAA Reviews|publisher=[[Mathematical Association of America]]|date=September 2016|first=Tom|last=Schulte|title=Review}}</ref>

In 1980 she was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]].<ref>[http://www.amstat.org/awards/fellowslist.cfm View/Search Fellows of the ASA] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160616161612/https://www.amstat.org/awards/fellowslist.cfm |date=2016-06-16 }}, accessed 2016-09-24.</ref> She is also a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]], a winner of the [[American Statistical Association Founders Award]],<ref name="stonybrook"/> and the 2006 winner of the Geoffrey Marshall Mentoring Award of the Northeastern Association of Graduate Schools.<ref name="hats"/>
